question: If the proportionate change in the demand is equal to the proportionate change in the price, the demand is said to be:
solution:
The correct answer is **unitary elastic demand.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Unitary elastic demand:**

 
 
• In unitary elastic demand, the percentage change in quantity demanded is exactly equal to the percentage change in price.
 
• This means that total revenue remains constant when the price changes.
 
• For example, if the price of a product increases by 10%, the quantity demanded will decrease by 10%.
 
• This concept is crucial for businesses in financial enterprises to understand how changes in pricing can affect their revenue.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Perfectly inelastic demand:**

 
 
• In perfectly inelastic demand, the quantity demanded does not change at all when the price changes.
 
• Goods with perfectly inelastic demand are typically necessities with no close substitutes.
 
 
 
• **Relatively elastic demand:**
 
 
• In relatively elastic demand, the percentage change in quantity demanded is greater than the percentage change in price.
 
• Consumers are highly responsive to price changes for these goods.
 
 
 
• **Relatively inelastic demand:**
 
 
• In relatively inelastic demand, the percentage change in quantity demanded is less than the percentage change in price.
 
• Consumers are less responsive to price changes for these goods.
